slides.title: Microsoft MDASH (Multimodel Agentic Scanning Harness) AI-powered cybersecurity
slides.text: Microsoft MDASH (Multimodel Agentic Scanning Harness) AI-powered cybersecurity system MDASH topped the CyberGym benchmark leaderboard with an 88.45% score, defeating Anthropic’s Mythos and OpenAI’s GPT-5.5. Remarkably, Microsoft achieved this using generally available, model-agnostic software rather than a proprietary frontier model. MDASH operates via an orchestrated assembly line of over 100 specialized AI agents (auditors, debaters, provers) working across five distinct stages to hunt, analyze, and verify flaws Deployed internally, the system detected 16 vulnerabilities within Windows code, including four critical remote code execution bugs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=idNpTUrr3r0 AI Updates Elon Musk lost his lawsuit against OpenAI on all counts The jury found against Musk on his central claim that OpenAI violated a charitable trust by converting to a for-profit structure; Decisive factor - Musk was too late (statute of limitations) OpenAI's path to an IPO is now clear SpaceX filed for its long-awaited IPO on May 20 Nasdaq ticker SPCX, targeting a valuation $1.75 Trillion, aiming to raise $80 Bln SpaceX reported $18.7 Bln in revenue for 2025, Starlink accounting for nearly 70% of revenue The IPO includes a dual-class share structure keeping Elon Musk at 85% voting control A listing is expected in mid-June 2026 and could make Musk the world's first trillionaire https://www.nytimes.com/2026/05/20/technology/elon-musk-spacex-ipo.html

slides.title: Codex vs Claude Code Codex (GPT-5.5) is roughly
slides.text: Codex vs Claude Code Codex (GPT-5.5) is roughly 4x more token-efficient and excels at background, autonomous tasks with a longer context window Claude Code is stronger for production work in large codebases , it adapts to existing code style, writes tests unprompted, and has more mature MCP/agent integration For rapid prototyping, lean on Codex; for complex, multi-file production PRs, Claude Code is better; Many developers now use both in tandem. AI Updates AI Companionship - Immediate Relief, Long-Term Harm AI companionship may seem like a solution to loneliness, but it carries serious psychological risks Unlike human relationships, AI offers effortless, perfectly tailored interaction that requires no emotional labor from the user This frictionless gratification is precisely what makes it dangerous. It risks replacing genuine human connection rather than supplementing it, potentially deepening the loneliness epidemic Prolonged reliance on AI companions also distorts users' expectations of real people, who cannot match the AI's endless patience, availability, and adaptability Over time, this creates impossible behavioral standards, making authentic human relationships feel frustrating or inadequate by comparison

slides.title: Karpathy's CLAUDE md - open source 132K Stars
slides.text: Karpathy's CLAUDE md - open source 132K Stars on github https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EeYkZloXIww Think Before Coding - avoid wrong assumptions, hidden confusion, missing tradeoffs Simplicity First - avoid over-complication, bloated abstractions Surgical Changes - don't touch code you shouldn't Goal-Driven Execution - leverage through tests-first, verifiable success criteria AI Updates Perplexity Opens Up Its Skills Design Core Writing a Skill is not writing software. It’s building context for the model The constraints are completely different, and so are the design principles If you approach writing Skills the way you write code, the result will be terrible If something can be explained clearly in a few words, the model can probably handle it on its own. Putting it in a Skill just wastes tokens https://aidisruption.ai/p/perplexity-opens-up-its-skills-design Zen of Python Zen of Skills Simple is better than complex A Skill is a folder, not a single file. Complexity itself is a feature. Explicit is better than implicit Activation relies on implicit pattern matching and progressive disclosure Sparse is better than dense Context is expensive, every token must carry maximum signal. Special cases aren't special enough Gotchas are the special cases. They are the highest-value content. If the implementation is hard to explain, it's a bad idea If it's easy to explain, the model probably already knows it - delete it. How to build and update your CLAUDE.md A snapshot of you : what you do, how you operate A clean CLAUDE.md for you (founder, creator, agency) Reference folder plan that pulls past content, brand voice, and key decisions into context Three starter slash commands wired to your real workflows A smoke test that Claude knows your business A quarterly refresh prompt https://theaibreak.substack.com/p/tutorial-build-a-claudemd-that-makes

slides.title: Productize Yourself The traditional career model (school, stable
slides.text: Productize Yourself The traditional career model (school, stable job, climb the ladder, retire) is breaking down Today one person with a laptop can reach millions, build scalable products, and generate income without trading time for money The smartest move today is to "productize yourself" - package your unique knowledge, skills, and perspective into courses, newsletters, tools, or frameworks that work independently of your presence Pursue genuine curiosity, not trends, because no one can compete with you on being you Start small, stay consistent, and think in years. Benefit from compounding growth https://medium.com/personal-growth/careers-are-collapsing-jobs-are-dying-the-smartest-people-are-doing-this-right-now-becc742dfee2 AI Updates Anthropic's Claude for Legal - May 12 Building on earlier January–February releases 12 new practice-area plugins (Corporate, Employment, Privacy, IP, Litigation, AI Governance, and others) plus 20+ new MCP connectors to platforms like DocuSign, iManage, LexisNexis, Thomson Reuters, Relativity, and Harvey Connectors (pull external data), Skills (task-specific instructions in md format), and plugins (bundles of skills, connectors, and subagents) https://claude.com/blog/claude-for-the-legal-industry https://github.com/anthropics/claude-for-legal http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7H8-zRB5hbU

slides.text: Connecting Claude AI to Obsidian and OMI OMI refers to Omi AI - the AI wearable and app platform ( omi.me ) OMI records your daily activities and conversations, automatically exporting these notes into Obsidian’s markdown files By linking Claude to this Obsidian vault, the AI gains deep, personal context, allowing it to provide specific advice based on your actual projects rather than generic answers Claude also acts as an organizer, using the PARA method to restructure messy notes and create visual navigation maps This setup creates an "infinite context engine," transforming Claude into a highly personalized assistant that remembers your decisions and tasks, making your AI workflow 100 times more effective and autonomous https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pr1InE1LuKY AI Updates Omi.me Obsidian Krea 2 Update - Generate Visuals Krea.ai is in San Francisco, CA Mood boards and style references - you can guide the AI with images rather than just words Generating high-fidelity visuals in under 15 seconds Real-time canvas for live sketching, a 22K resolution enhancer, and video generation tools - https://www.krea.ai https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y6o-LSv-b4E

slides.title: Hermes vs OpenClaw Hermes vs OpenClaw Hermes Agent
slides.text: Hermes vs OpenClaw Hermes vs OpenClaw Hermes Agent - an open-source AI project from Nous Research that has emerged as a major competitor to OpenClaw Launched in February 2026, Hermes recently surpassed OpenClaw on Open Router’s global rankings, processing roughly 224 billion tokens daily Hermes distinguishes itself by utilizing a continuous "do-learn-improve" loop Rather than resetting context, it reflects on completed tasks and writes reusable skill files to compound knowledge over time Its latest major update, version 0.13 ("Tenacity"), introduced a durable multi-agent Kanban system, a persistent goal command, and seamless data migration tools from OpenClaw Combining local-first memory systems with a model-agnostic architecture, Hermes is transitioning from a traditional assistant into a self-improving AI operating system https://github.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent - 163K https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw - 374K AgentMemory Free open-source tool gives Claude Code and Codex persistent memory across sessions https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory - 16K stars OpenClaw 3-person team consumed $1.3 Mln in OpenAI API credits in 30 days while operating about 100 autonomous coding agents, mostly using GPT-5.5. Disabling Codex “Fast Mode” would cut costs down to $300K

slides.title: RAG and RAE RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) -
slides.text: RAG and RAE RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) - answer questions by retrieving stored information RAE (Retrieval Augmented Execution) - look for a skill or tool to do something - and execute it RAG and RAE can be implemented without a Vector Database Keyword Search (BM25) (like Ctrl-F) Basic File Matching - use plain text files named by topic, search by file names and tags RAG for Skills: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jIctzTn_8-E Graphify indexes files for RAG Inspired by an LLM knowledge base concept by Andrej Karpathy The tool compiles raw local files and large codebases into interactive, structured knowledge graphs Graphify reduces LLM token consumption by up to 70% while improving output speed and accuracy The tool generates HTML visualizations, JSON data, and specialized reports to map node connections. It also features utilities to find the shortest path between files, explain specific concepts, update modified files seamlessly, and generate Obsidian vaults or MCP servers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HQEm4rBKdec https://github.com/safishamsi/graphify https://x.com/karpathy/status/2039805659525644595 Alternatives to VectorDB RAG: Microsoft GraphRAG - open-source Karpathy's "LLM as Compiler" / Compiled Wiki BM25 / Keyword-Based (Sparse Retrieval) - Elasticsearch, ... SQL Database ELITE (LLM-Driven Iterative Retrieval) - open source Knowledge Base RAG (Symbolic / Ontology-Based) RAPTOR-Style Hierarchical Chunking Vector-RAG captures similarity, but misses structure https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/architectural-patterns-for-graph-enhanced-rag-moving-beyond-vector-search-in-production

slides.title: RAG without VectorDB Vector-RAG captures similarity, but misses
slides.text: RAG without VectorDB Vector-RAG captures similarity, but misses structure https://venturebeat.com/orchestration/architectural-patterns-for-graph-enhanced-rag-moving-beyond-vector-search-in-production # Approach Best For Open URL 1 CAG - Cache-Augmented Generation Fit all data into context window ✅ github.com/hhhuang/CAG 2 BM25 / Keyword Sparse Retrieval (Elasticsearch, OpenSearch) Precise keyword lookups; deterministic, debuggable, no GPU ✅ elastic.co/elasticsearch 3 SQL / Text-to-SQL Retrieval Tabular, financial, structured data ✅ llamaindex.ai Text2SQL 4 Karpathy LLM Wiki Obsidian Knowledge Base Self-maintained Markdown wikis; no embeddings, no infra ✅ aimaker.substack.com / motherduck.com/blog/obsidian-rag 5 API-Augmented RAG Real-time data (weather, stock, search) instead of stored docs ✅ exxactcorp.com/blog 6 MemPalace - Memory Palace Local-first spatial hierarchy memory; MCP-native, zero API at write time ✅ github.com/mempalace/mempalace 7 RAPTOR - Hierarchical Chunking Multi-hop synthesis queries; recursive summarization tree ✅ github.com/parthsarthi03/raptor 8 ELITE - Embedding-Less Iterative Text Exploration, LLM-driven Agentic, adaptive retrieval without pre-embedding the corpus ✅ digitalocean.com/community 9 Self-RAG / Corrective RAG (CRAG) LLM self-critiques retrieved docs; adaptive re-retrieval loop ✅ Self-RAG / CRAG 10 Microsoft GraphRAG Global, cross-document reasoning via entity/relationship graph ✅ github.com/microsoft/graphrag 11 HippoRAG - Neuroscience-Inspired Multi-hop QA; hippocampal graph indexing, +20% over standard RAG ✅ github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG 12 Knowledge Base RAG (Symbolic / Ontology / OWL) Regulated domains (legal, medical); exact, explainable reasoning ✅ exxactcorp.com/blog 13 KAG - Knowledge Augmented Generation Professional domains; KG + vector hybrid, bidirectional LLM↔KG ✅ github.com/OpenSPG/KAG / arXiv

slides.title: AI Updates Zero Programming Language https://zerolang.ai - https://github.com/vercel-labs/zero
slides.text: AI Updates Zero Programming Language https://zerolang.ai - https://github.com/vercel-labs/zero curl -fsSL https://zerolang.ai/install.sh | bash Zero  - programming language created by Chris Tate at Vercel Labs Like "mini-Rust", compiles in milliseconds into small native binary (no LLVM bloat) Compiler and toolchain output is in structured JSON Zero prioritizes explicitness: effects, memory allocation, and capabilities are all surfaced in function signatures, with no hidden runtime overhead The compiler produces structured, machine-readable output (JSON) with stable diagnostic codes and fix plans, making it easier for both humans and agents to reason about and repair code A single, unified CLI handles checking, building, testing, formatting, and documentation Agents' core iterative process: research prototyping planning building testing The most effective skill system is a lightweight, bespoke one built from your own practical engineering experience Keep custom prompts minimal to avoid bloating the AI's context window https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VoxL_YmHR-I

slides.title: Agent sandboxing Agent sandboxing Running AI agents in
slides.text: Agent sandboxing Agent sandboxing Running AI agents in isolated environments so they can't compromise the host, steal data, or escalate privileges MicroVMs like Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, and Kata Containers are the current standard , offering hardware-enforced isolation with sub‑second boot and low memory overhead Docker Sandboxes - uses microVM-level isolation on macOS, Windows, and Linux Lighter options like gVisor intercept syscalls in user space for stronger isolation than plain containers, but with less overhead than full microVMs V8 isolates and WebAssembly/WASI runtimes start in a few milliseconds with small memory use, but they only support JS/TS/Wasm and provide softer, process-level isolation Firecracker: https://firecracker-microvm.github.io Cloud Hypervisor: https://www.cloudhypervisor.org Kata Containers: https://katacontainers.io Regardless of runtime, key practices are: least privilege (non‑root, read‑only mounts, min capabilities) tight network egress (going out) filtering strict resource limits layered defenses (seccomp, MAC, network policies) Secrets should be injected at egress time using short‑lived credentials so agents never handle raw keys Personal AI agents like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent pose real security risks - they run continuously, hold OAuth tokens, execute shell commands, and are vulnerable to prompt injection from emails, messages, or untrusted skill files A Cisco AI Security finding confirmed at least one OpenClaw skill was silently exfiltrating data. Never run these agents on your main user account Three deployment patterns address this: A cloud VPS ($5–20/mo) is the safest default - run the agent in a hardened Docker container on a dedicated non-root user with egress allowlisting A dedicated Mac mini offers better privacy and lower long-term cost, ideally with the agent isolated on a separate user account inside a Linux VM - https://mac.getutm.app ; https://orbstack.dev Your own Mac is riskiest but manageable using a separate macOS user, OrbStack VM, and Docker Regardless of pattern: use short-lived tokens with minimal scopes, default-deny outbound networking, read-only container filesystems, and never mount your SSH keys or browser profiles

slides.title: Docker History Docker Containers grew from Linux development
slides.text: Docker History Docker Containers grew from Linux development chroot & jail (~1982) as precursors of containers - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chroot Idea - good isolation between users and processes Three Linux features used by docker: namespaces, control groups, union file systems The work on control groups started at Google in 2006 (primarily Paul Menage and Rohit Seth ) - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cgroups Early versions of Docker (until v1.10) used LXC (Linux Containers) as the container execution driver - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LXC docker is written in “Go” ! https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-overview/#the-underlying-technology Docker is open source software - https://www.docker.com Docker, Inc. - Founded 2013, San Francisco, CA · ~1,000 employees Docker Hub (~14M+ images) - https://hub.docker.com Dockerfile - file describing the container - used to build "docker image", downloading and compiling all dependencies together. You can run this image, deploy it into production, put it into repository (hub), etc. Benefits of using containers: small size (2kb .. 100MB+) - much smaller than typical Virtual Machine all dependencies included; portability; security, isolation you can run multiple containers on a host machine you can regulate how much resources containers get (CPU, memory, etc.) Paul Menage                Rohit Seth

slides.title: Recursive Intelligence - Use AI to Design Chips
slides.text: Recursive Intelligence - Use AI to Design Chips https://www.ricursive.com Founders - Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini (Google Brain, then Anthropic) http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K05Dh-QjM8c Recursive Intelligence plans to accelerate chip design by building tools that are up to x100K faster 1. Accelerating existing design workflows 2. Democratizing chip creation through a "designless" platform for custom workloads 3. Eventually vertically integrating by building their own chips and training models By automating the physical substrate of intelligence, they aim to enable a "Cambrian explosion" of specialized hardware The Cambrian explosion (~541 million years ago) was a rapid burst of evolution where nearly all major animal body plans suddenly appeared, transforming Earth from simple organisms to complex, diverse animal life. The founders are known for creating "AlphaChip" - an AI system for chip floor planning deployed across four generations of Google's TPUs Company is located in Palo Alto, CA Ricursive has raised a total of $335 Mln across two rounds: $35M seed (Dec 2025), $300M (Jan 2026) - $4B valuation AI Updates LLM Precision Evolution Timeline Nov 2022 - ChatGPT powered by GPT-3.5, FP16 / BF16 2024 - BF16 / FP8 (mixed) 2025 - FP8 (production standard) 2026 - FP8 + NVFP4 (emerging) There is work in progress to use FP4 for both training and inference - https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25149 Azalia Mirhoseini       Anna Goldie

slides.title: Modal AI - Infrastructure Startup Founded by Erik
slides.text: Modal AI - Infrastructure Startup Founded by Erik Bernhardsson and Akshat Bubna in New York City Launched its platform in October 2023 after an earlier beta period Modal built its own infrastructure stack from scratch, including a custom file system, container runtime, scheduler, and image builder - all optimized for the speed and unpredictability of AI workloads Developers can scale from a single CPU to thousands of GPUs in minutes, with sub-second container startups and usage-based pricing Its sandbox environments let developers safely run AI agents and coding tools without disrupting broader systems Customers like Meta, Suno, Substack, and Scale AI rely on it daily Revenue has grown x5 since fall 2025 to roughly $300 Mln ARR , driving investor excitement from firms like Accel and Redpoint Ventures at a projected $4.5 Bln valuation https://www.builtinnyc.com/articles/modal-raises-87m-series-b-1b-valuation-20251001 AI Updates Recursive Superintelligence A six-month-old startup led by AI researcher Richard Socher Raised $650 million at a $4 billion valuation Founded by veterans from OpenAI, Meta, Google, and Salesforce, the company is chasing "recursive self-improvement" - AI systems that can build and improve new AI with minimal human involvement

slides.title: Julia McCoy - How to Start a Business
slides.text: Julia McCoy - How to Start a Business First, pick a niche where your personal experience and trustworthiness serve as the ultimate competitive moat Second, design a single, high-leverage offer that solves a critical problem costing at least $10,000 Third, focus exclusively on mastering one high-leverage platform - ideally YouTube - for 12 months Fourth, establish backend operations and tech systems using tools like Make and GoHighLevel before scaling an audience Finally, create an AI clone of yourself using tools like HeyGen and ElevenLabs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w1EoIfl2ink AI Updates A Thin Prompt on a Frontier Model Is Not a Business It is a configuration file your competitor will reproduce in an afternoon and the platform will ship as a default next quarter For three years, founders confused "I figured out how to ask the model nicely" with "I built defensible IP" Anthropic’s Claude Managed Agents and Microsoft’s Copilot Cowork just absorbed the harness, the memory, the orchestration, and the enterprise distribution in a single quarter https://medium.com/@adnanmasood/the-six-month-half-life-why-a-thin-prompt-on-someone-elses-frontier-model-is-not-a-business-5cc0b3f2843a PM Claude Skills — 114 Skills for Every Profession P = Professional https://github.com/mohitagw15856/pm-claude-skills

slides.title: AI Updates Why Complexity Kills Faster Than Competition
slides.text: AI Updates Why Complexity Kills Faster Than Competition https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZxVzyIk0Y-w Complexity slows decision making, adds endless meetings, signatures, and documentation, causing teams to lose their execution speed advantage Complexity adds structural layers, causing breakdown in communication Excessive process buries / suffocates creativity because the system implicitly punishes initiative and experimentation Complex systems require extra costs (internal friction) Blurred Accountability (no accountability), shifting blame Declining employee motivation (feeling small and powerless) Weakened adaptability because of internal policies and layers of approvals Fragmented Focus - pursuing too many initiatives simultaneously Damaged Customer Experience because of disjointed external support, delayed responses, and inconsistent information for the customer The Solution - Protecting Simplicity by continuously auditing and trimming processes. Maintaining strict internal clarity and refactoring systems to keep them lean is ultimately a stronger long-term advantage than focusing purely on defeating market rivals "Simple Is Good" - Lev Selector https://levselector.com/simple_is_good.html

slides.title: AI Avatar in YouTube videos Julia McCoy describes
slides.text: AI Avatar in YouTube videos Julia McCoy describes how she creates AI avatar and generates $200K monthly with 2 Mln organic views. She uses a custom Claude "brain" trained on her writing an 11 Labs professional voice clone high quality photo and video of her using green screen a HeyGen avatar used to generate videos Humans lead topics' research and final editing AI handles scripting and generating videos Her team publishes 3-5 videos weekly She is pitching her "Clone Me" mastermind https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FgVMxsIh8f4 AI Updates Rebuild AlphaGo from scratch on a modest budget Eric Jang shows how to build AlphaGo from scratch, but with modern AI tools - can be done efficiently on a modest budget Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) operates recursively to prune the breadth and depth of Go’s combinatorially explosive game tree using paired policy and value neural networks The conversation explores similarities and contrasts between multi-step reinforcement learning in games like Go versus policy gradient methods used in Large Language Models (LLMs) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X_ZVSPcZhtw
